Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation and test-infrastructure engineer with 7 years of experience, including ownership of CI/CD pipelines and ephemeral test environments for three product teams. Hands-on experience with GitLab CI, Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, alongside personal infrastructure projects using Terraform and GitOps. Strong record of improving pipeline performance and reliability, documenting technical workflows, and supporting teams adopting shared tooling. Developing cloud and infrastructure-as-code experience through personal projects and ongoing Kubernetes study.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level experience), k3s, Argo CD
Infrastructure as Code & Automation: Terraform (personal projects), Ansible (basic), Bash, Python
Monitoring & Data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL, GitLab API
Cloud & Networking: Hetzner VPS (personal project), AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning), Traefik, TLS certificate management with cert-manager
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Other: Linux, Git, Java (test code), SQL

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering builds, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by approximately 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request environments for the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster; environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built a Python, PostgreSQL and Grafana dashboard using CI results to highlight flaky tests by team and help teams identify priority fixes.
- Wrote Bash and Python tools for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and authored an internal guide to CI workflows used in team onboarding.
- Mentored two QA interns in 2023. Work with namespace-level Kubernetes access; the platform team operates the shared cluster.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects through manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Operated a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam scheduled for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible CV with clear progression from QA automation into test infrastructure and DevOps. The Professional Summary is appropriately candid about the candidate's current level, while the experience section uses concrete ownership statements and measurable outcomes: pipeline duration decreased from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs fell by approximately 30%, and flaky tests decreased from 7% to below 1%. The selected infrastructure project adds useful evidence of Kubernetes, GitOps, observability, TLS certificate management and Terraform exposure. The document is well structured, professional and easy to scan. Its main content limitation is that several role-relevant areas—system design, security awareness, stakeholder alignment and networking depth—are not demonstrated, although these are primarily candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional section headings, reverse-chronological experience, simple text formatting and ATS-friendly bullets. It contains relevant keywords including GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Linux, AWS EC2, S3, TLS and cert-manager. The strongest ATS evidence is in the Odrava role and the infrastructure project section. AI screening probability is moderate to good for junior/mid-level DevOps or platform roles, but lower for this specific contractor role because the ad heavily prioritises strong Terraform and Terragrunt, cloud environment operation, system design, mTLS, security and production-grade infrastructure ownership. The phrase "Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer" is somewhat stronger than the documented professional experience, which is mainly QA test infrastructure plus personal cloud projects. The current Skills categories may also cause a recruiter or screening model to overestimate the extent of production cloud and networking experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with infrastructure ownership, CI/CD, Kubernetes-based environment deployment, observability, Linux, analytical problem-solving, documentation and technical enablement. It also provides credible evidence of ownership and communication through managing pipelines for three teams, writing the CI onboarding guide and supporting team adoption of shared tooling. AWS is shown only as basic personal learning, which is acceptable as a stated nice-to-have exposure but not equivalent to professional AWS operation. The candidate's material does not demonstrate strong Terraform, Terragrunt, system architecture/system design, mTLS, practical security ownership, IoT or remote-device integration, virtual machines, production on-call or direct cloud production operations. These are capability gaps rather than defects that can be fixed through wording. The document is a truthful and reasonably well-positioned application for a junior or mid-level infrastructure/DevOps pathway, but it is not yet a strong match for a contractor expected to design and operate fleet-connectivity infrastructure from the start.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the boundary between professional and personal cloud experience even more explicit. Replace "Developing cloud and infrastructure-as-code experience through personal projects and ongoing Kubernetes study" with wording such as: "Professional experience focuses on CI/CD and Kubernetes-based test infrastructure; cloud and infrastructure-as-code experience comes from personal Terraform, Hetzner and AWS learning projects." This prevents the target title from overstating production cloud experience.

2. In the Technical Skills section, rename "Cloud & Networking" to "Cloud, Networking & TLS (personal/learning where noted)" and keep the existing qualifiers directly beside the relevant technologies. For example: "Hetzner VPS (personal project), AWS EC2 and S3 (basic personal learning), Traefik, TLS certificate management with cert-manager." This preserves ATS keywords while making the experience level immediately clear.

3. In the Odrava Health Software experience section, strengthen the existing evidence for technical leadership and communication by revising the documentation bullet to: "Authored an internal guide to CI workflows used in team onboarding, helping product teams adopt shared pipeline and test-environment tooling." This uses the job ad's stakeholder and adoption language without claiming formal leadership that is not documented.

4. In the Odrava role, make the infrastructure ownership boundary as prominent as the technology itself. Retain the final sentence about namespace-level access, but revise it to: "Deployed Helm-based test environments with namespace-level Kubernetes access; the platform team owns operation of the shared cluster." This is clearer and avoids any possible interpretation that the candidate operated the cluster at platform level.

5. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section, add the existing GitLab API evidence to the Flaky Test Dashboard work if space permits, because it demonstrates integration and automation relevant to platform engineering. For example, add a project entry: "Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023 — Collected CI results through the GitLab API into PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team; flaky rate fell from 7% to below 1%." Do not imply that this was production platform observability beyond test metrics.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, clear, professional CV with good evidence of measurable impact. Metrics such as the reduction from 38 to 14 minutes, the 30% runner-cost reduction, and the reduction in flaky tests make the achievements convincing. The main limitation is not poor writing but the candidate's limited direct evidence of production cloud infrastructure, strong Terraform/Terragrunt work, system design, networking security, and operational ownership required by this particular contractor role.

However, the candidate's material shows gaps against several core requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt; broad cloud environment design and operation; systems architecture and system design; mTLS and broader network design; practical security awareness; production operational ownership; and IoT, automotive, or remote-device integration. TLS certificate management with cert-manager is shown, but mTLS is not. The CV is therefore a credible adjacent or junior-to-mid platform/infrastructure profile, but not a strong match for a contractor expected to shape a fleet-connectivity platform from the start.
